front: Which OSI layer is responsible for managing sessions between applications?
Which OSI layer is responsible for providing network services directly to applications (HTTP, FTP live here)?
Which OSI layer is responsible for breaking data into frames and physical addressing (MAC addresses)?
What are the 8 ethernet frame sections:
back: Preamble — alternating 1s and 0s that signal to the receiver that a message is coming. Start Frame Delimiter (SFD) — alternating 1s and 0s ending in two consecutive 1s to mark the exact start of the data. Destination Address — recipient MAC address Source Address — the MAC address of the sending device (always unicast). Length Data Padding — extra bits added if the data doesn't meet the minimum frame size requirement. CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) — an error detection code at the end used to verify the data wasn't corrupted.

front: What sort of an address is the source address in the datalink layer?
Unicast, Multicast, broadcast. Whats the difference in the datalink layer?
back: - Unicast sending to a single destination. - multicast is send to predefined group in a LAN - Broadcast sends to every node in a LAN

front: In the datalink layer which bit of which byte in a mac addresss determines if that address is unicast or multicast?
back: The last bit of the 1st byte.

front: A device has the MAC address A2:3F:45:67:89:AB. Is this unicast or multicast?
back: A in binary is 1010 — last bit is 0 → Unicast

front: A device has the MAC address B1:2C:3D:4E:5F:6A. Is this unicast or multicast?
back: B in binary is 1011 — last bit is 1 → Multicast
